newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy mini-budget expected March 27 - newspapers.
newsitem.headline: Italy mini-budget expected March 27 - newspapers.

text.p: The Italian government is likely to present its mini-budget on March 27 after the release of quarterly state accounts which are expected by the end of the week, Italian newspapers said on Wednesday.

Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said the quarterly accounts would be presented to parliament by the end of the week, while daily Corriere della Sera said the data would be presented on Thursday or the day after at the latest.
All said the extra budget measures, expected to be 14-15 trillion lire, would be announced on March 27, with the Corriere saying the amount was likely to be just under 15 trillion.

The government has said it intends to announce extra deficit-cutting measures soon in order to reduce the 1997 budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product, in line with Maastricht criteria for joining European monetary union.

The Corriere said part of the measures -- a levy on funds built up by companies for severance payments -- would raise seven trillion lire, with more pressure on state sector companies than those in private hands.

It said as far as pensions were concerned, the plan so far was for a 1.5 percent contribution from people who have retired early and 0.5 percent for those receiving more than one million lire in benefits a month, as well as a levy on workers contributing to pensions.
The Corriere said the government was likely to raise the number of years teachers worked before they could draw a pension to 32 from 30 years.
It said the Treasury had been pressing for the introduction of payments on in-patient hospital care and home visits by doctors.
